description: We are 6 girls passioned by space and aviation !
summary:
We developed an interactive educational app that brings NASA’s history to life for children through the stories of lost and forgotten objects and missions. Guided by five “Space Girls,” young explorers travel through six missions, each built around mini-games that turn learning into play.

Its narrative thread makes it unique: behind every mission stands a real woman whose contribution to space exploration is brought into the spotlight. Children don’t just discover artifacts and events, they also meet the often overlooked people who made them possible.

The platform comes in two versions: a full-length one, used as a pedagogical resource during science days, and a “split” version, mission by mission, designed for exhibitions and science centers such as the Cité de l’Espace, where visits are shorter.

This directly answers the challenge, as many NASA missions, and the women behind them, have faded from collective memory. By combining storytelling, interactivity and play, the app makes this heritage accessible to young audiences, so discovery feels like an adventure rather than a lesson.

It matters because it preserves space history at risk of being forgotten while offering young learners, especially girls, relatable role models in science and engineering. By making history fun and inclusive, it sparks curiosity, shows that space belongs to everyone, and inspires the next generation of explorers.
details:
The Compass of Firsts is an interactive, story-driven web game for children aged 10 to 12, created for the challenge “Abandoned but Not Forgotten”. It turns six machines that NASA left in space into six playable missions, and it reveals the women who made them possible. Guided by five heroines, the Space Girls, and by the “Compass of Firsts”, the player travels through space history: the Apollo Lunar Module descent stages left on the Moon (1969), the Pioneer 10 and 11 probes now drifting out of the Solar System (1972), Sojourner, the first rover on Mars (1997), the Dawn spacecraft still orbiting Ceres (2007), the Kepler telescope saved by the pressure of sunlight (2009), and Ingenuity, the first aircraft to fly on another planet (2021).

The missions follow a chronological order linked by a scientific thread, “further, longer, smarter”, with a timeline at the bottom of the screen. Each mission combines narrated dialogue, quizzes and mini-games based on real science, such as detecting a planet with the transit method. The five characters speak with our own voices, as each team member recorded one of them. Each completed mission earns a badge and fills a branch of the compass. Once all six badges are collected, the Grand Final reveals the women behind the machines, such as MiMi Aung, Donna Shirley and Margaret Hamilton, and the player receives a personalised diploma. All images and facts come from NASA open resources: the NASA Image and Video Library, the NSSDC database and the NASA Science mission pages.

Both versions of the game are available from a single website, https://space-girls-the-compass-of-firsts.netlify.app. The Classroom Edition offers the full six-mission journey and is designed to be played together in class. The Museum Edition is split by mission, with one interactive station per machine that can be placed next to an exhibit.

Space Girls helps children learn by playing, because facts discovered through stories and challenges are easier to remember. It also gives them role models by putting women engineers and scientists at the center of the story. Finally, it highlights the human factor: behind every lost machine there are teams who designed it, fought to save it and said goodbye to it. The game runs for free in any web browser, with nothing to install. Our next steps are to test it with real classes, adapt it for science centres, translate it into more languages and add new missions and role models.

The project was developed as a web application in HTML, CSS and JavaScript and is hosted on Netlify. We used Claude, an AI assistant from Anthropic, to help us with the coding. The scripts, the storytelling and the character voices were created by our team
